sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: This is from Twitter.
sentences.zh: 这条来自推特。

sentences.en: Hey Roman Mars and 99PI.org, I have a burning question for you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼·马斯和99PI.org，我有个迫切的问题想问你们。

sentences.en: Why do U.S.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国

sentences.en: flags on military vehicles and uniforms always appear backwards?
sentences.zh: 军车和制服上的国旗总是反着的？

sentences.en: That's from Michael McAlpin.
sentences.zh: 这是迈克尔·麦卡尔平提的。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, they're only backwards part of the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它们只有在某些时候是反着的。

sentences.en: Military regulations state that when a flag is displayed,
sentences.zh: 军事条例规定，当悬挂旗帜时，

sentences.en: it must give the effect of that flag flying in the breeze
sentences.zh: 它必须呈现出旗帜在微风中飘扬的效果，

sentences.en: as if the person wearing it is moving forward.
sentences.zh: 就像穿戴它的人正在向前行进一样。

sentences.en: So if the patch is on the left arm, the flag is displayed as you normally think of it
sentences.zh: 所以如果徽章在左臂上，旗帜的显示方式就是你通常认为的那样，

sentences.en: with that blue star field in the upper left-hand corner.
sentences.zh: 蓝色星区在左上角。

sentences.en: But if the flag patch is on the right arm, it's the reverse side flag that's displayed
sentences.zh: 但如果旗帜徽章在右臂上，显示的则是反面旗帜，

sentences.en: with the blue star field in the upper right-hand corner.
sentences.zh: 蓝色星区在右上角。

sentences.en: The same goes for vehicles.
sentences.zh: 车辆也是如此。

sentences.en: The blue star field always points towards the front of the vehicle
sentences.zh: 蓝色星区总是指向车辆的前方，

sentences.en: as if it's flying and we're charging forward to victory.
sentences.zh: 就好像它在飘扬，而我们正冲向胜利。

sentences.en: So if you're looking at the right side of a tank or an aircraft,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看坦克或飞机的右侧，

sentences.en: you'll see the reverse flag.
sentences.zh: 你会看到反向的旗帜。

sentences.en: This is part two of the mini-stories episode where I interview the staff
sentences.zh: 这是“迷你故事”系列的第二部分，我采访了我们的员工，

sentences.en: about their favorite little design stories that don't quite fill out an entire episode
sentences.zh: 聊聊他们最喜欢的一些小设计故事，这些故事因为各种原因，

sentences.en: for whatever reason, but they are cool 99PI stories nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 不足以撑起一整集节目，但它们依然是精彩的99PI故事。

sentences.en: Plus, in between the staff stories, I'll be telling a few mini-stories
sentences.zh: 另外，在员工故事之间，我还会讲几个迷你故事，

sentences.en: suggested by you beautiful nerds who enjoy having me paraphrase Google search results
sentences.zh: 这些都是由你们这些可爱的书呆子建议的，你们很享受听我转述谷歌搜索结果，

sentences.en: and read them out loud.
sentences.zh: 并大声读出来。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Up first is senior editor Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 首先是资深编辑凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: My name is Katie Mingle, and I am the senior editor.
sentences.zh: 我叫凯蒂·明格尔，我是资深编辑。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: I do the same stuff that we all do in some ways, which is like
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，我做的事情和我们大家一样，比如

sentences.en: find stories and report on them and make them.
sentences.zh: 寻找故事、报道故事并制作它们。

sentences.en: But I also edit a lot.
sentences.zh: 但我还要做大量的编辑工作。

sentences.en: So I look at other people's stories on paper
sentences.zh: 所以我会审阅别人的文稿，

sentences.en: before they go to like a larger group edit, and I cut like five pages out of every story.
sentences.zh: 在它们进入更大规模的集体编辑之前，我会删掉每篇故事里大约五页的内容。

sentences.en: No, I probably cut like four minutes and sometimes do some restructuring
sentences.zh: 不，我大概会删掉四分钟的内容，有时还会做一些结构调整，

sentences.en: and just kind of try to get it ready so that it's a little more smooth
sentences.zh: 只是尽量让它准备得更完善，这样

sentences.en: when the whole group looks at it.
sentences.zh: 当整个团队审阅时，它会更顺畅一些。

sentences.en: And so even though we don't hear your voice in every story, you have worked on every story
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们没有在每个故事里听到你的声音，你也参与了每一个故事，

sentences.en: because you've edited almost every story that comes out of it.
sentences.zh: 因为你编辑了几乎每一个发布出来的故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm lurking behind every 99PI story.
sentences.zh: 我潜伏在每一个99PI故事的背后。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, but in addition to that, you do pitch stories.
sentences.zh: 那么，除此之外，你还会推介故事。

sentences.en: And so part of coming up with story ideas is basically just trolling around the internet,
sentences.zh: 构思故事创意的一部分，基本上就是四处浏览互联网，

sentences.en: trying to find things to turn things into stories.
sentences.zh: 试图找到能变成故事的东西。

sentences.en: And that's how this one came to you.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事就是这样来到你身边的。

sentences.en: Yeah, huge amounts of time just like following links.
sentences.zh: 是的，花了大量时间在网上顺着链接点来点去。

sentences.en: That's sort of like how this one came about.
sentences.zh: 这个故事大概就是这么来的。

sentences.en: And I ended up on this YouTube video about this place called the Biker Wall,
sentences.zh: 我最终看到了一个关于“拜克之墙”这个地方的YouTube视频，

sentences.en: which is in Newcastle, England.
sentences.zh: 它位于英国纽卡斯尔。

sentences.en: And it's being narrated by this woman wearing this amazing sort of double-breasted suit jacket.
sentences.zh: 视频由一位穿着令人惊叹的双排扣西装外套的女士解说。

sentences.en: And she's just super, super 80s.
sentences.zh: 她非常有80年代的感觉。

sentences.en: Her name's Beatrix Campbell.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫比阿特丽克斯·坎贝尔。

sentences.en: In the video, she's sort of walking around outside the Biker Wall or the Biker Estate.
sentences.zh: 在视频中，她走在拜克之墙或拜克住宅区外面。

sentences.en: It's big and it's small.
sentences.zh: 它既大又小。

sentences.en: It's cheap and cheerful.
sentences.zh: 它既便宜又令人愉快。

sentences.en: It's cheeky.
sentences.zh: 它很俏皮。

sentences.en: And it's clever.
sentences.zh: 而且很聪明。

sentences.en: I don't really know how it's big and small.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道它怎么能既大又小。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that ever we ever really figure that out.
sentences.zh: 而且我不确定我们是否真的弄明白了。

sentences.en: So the structure or the sort of estate that she's talking about,
sentences.zh: 所以她谈论的这个结构或住宅区，

sentences.en: it actually replaced an entire neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 实际上取代了整个街区。

sentences.en: So let me just give you a little background.
sentences.zh: 让我给你们一点背景信息。

sentences.en: In 1963, in Newcastle, England, a 17,000-resident, working-class neighborhood called Biker,
sentences.zh: 1963年，在英国纽卡斯尔，一个拥有17000名居民的工人阶级社区叫拜克，

sentences.en: so the same name as this new place, was demolished because it was considered a slum.
sentences.zh: 和这个新地方名字一样，因为它被认为是贫民窟而被拆除了。

sentences.en: And I think there were a lot of vacancies.
sentences.zh: 我想当时有很多空房。

sentences.en: And the neighborhood was made up of sort of Victorian row housing.
sentences.zh: 那个社区由维多利亚时代的联排房屋组成。

sentences.en: And, like, if you've ever seen the movie Billy Elliot, and you can, like, picture him sort of dancing through these, like, brick houses
sentences.zh: 如果你看过电影《跳出我天地》，你可以想象他穿过这些砖房跳舞的样子，

sentences.en: and really, really close together and narrow streets, that's the old biker.
sentences.zh: 房子靠得非常非常近，街道狭窄，那就是旧拜克。

sentences.en: That's the old biker.
sentences.zh: 那就是旧拜克。

sentences.en: And I think that movie was actually filmed really close to the old biker neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我想那部电影实际上就是在离旧拜克社区很近的地方拍摄的。

sentences.en: Street by street, the old slums were cleared while street by street, the new biker was built.
sentences.zh: 旧的贫民窟被逐条街道清理，而新的拜克被逐条街道建造起来。

sentences.en: So, yeah, in place of the old neighborhood of brick row houses, this architect named Ralph Erskine built the new place,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在旧的砖砌联排房屋社区原址上，一位名叫拉尔夫·厄斯金的建筑师建造了新地方，

sentences.en: which is called Biker Wall, or sometimes Biker Estate.
sentences.zh: 它被称为拜克之墙，有时也叫拜克住宅区。

sentences.en: And it's a community of public housing that is enclosed by this great big wall of apartments.
sentences.zh: 这是一个公共住房社区，被这堵巨大的公寓墙所包围。

sentences.en: The wall is a mile and a half long, and it provides a barrier to winds coming kind of off the North Sea and also highway noise.
sentences.zh: 这堵墙有一英里半长，它为来自北海的风和高速公路的噪音提供了屏障。

sentences.en: There's, like, a big freeway or expressway nearby.
sentences.zh: 附近有一条大型高速公路或快速路。

sentences.en: And it kind of creates this sort of microclimate within the community.
sentences.zh: 它在社区内创造了一种微气候。

sentences.en: So it's basically this big wall that sort of wraps around these other buildings and closing them.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上就是这堵大墙，环绕着其他建筑，将它们包围起来。

sentences.en: And Campbell, she has some very, like, vivid descriptions.
sentences.zh: 坎贝尔，她有一些非常生动的描述。

sentences.en: But she says the way it's constructed and laid out kind of reminds her of a pomegranate.
sentences.zh: 她说它的建造和布局方式让她想起了石榴。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a pomegranate.
sentences.zh: 它有点像石榴。

sentences.en: It's fruity, hard edges, and soft, sweet places inside.
sentences.zh: 它有果实，坚硬的外壳，里面有柔软甜美的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, and if you're feeling, like, at all, like, that was a little sexual, it gets, like, there's more.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你觉得这听起来有点色情，还有更劲爆的。

sentences.en: But what does all this mean for architecture?
sentences.zh: 但这对于建筑意味着什么？

sentences.en: Is it modernist or postmodernist or what?
sentences.zh: 它是现代主义还是后现代主义，还是什么？

sentences.en: For sure, it abolishes aggressive phallic architecture, all those gray erections which puncture the skyline.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，它废除了咄咄逼人的阳具建筑，那些刺破天际线的灰色勃起物。

sentences.en: Maybe it's vulval architecture.
sentences.zh: 也许它是阴道建筑。

sentences.en: It's round.
sentences.zh: 它是圆的。

sentences.en: It goes with the contours of the landscape.
sentences.zh: 它顺应了景观的轮廓。

sentences.en: It's an enclosure rather than a disclosure, full of nukes and crannies, layers and levels and surprises.
sentences.zh: 它是一种包围而非披露，充满了角落和缝隙、层次和水平以及惊喜。

sentences.en: Woo!
sentences.zh: 呜！

sentences.en: Nukes and crannies.
sentences.zh: 角落和缝隙。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, yeah, if you didn't hear that, it abolishes aggressive phallic architecture and those gray erections that puncture the skyline for a vulval architecture.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你没听清，她说它废除了咄咄逼人的阳具建筑和那些刺破天际线的灰色勃起物，取而代之的是一种阴道建筑。

sentences.en: F*** those gray erections.
sentences.zh: 去他的灰色勃起物。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Yes, so I found this place and I was sort of like, I want to put this on the air basically just to get this lady and her vulval architecture theories on our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我发现了这个地方，我当时就想，我一定要把它搬上电台，主要是为了让这位女士和她的阴道建筑理论出现在我们的播客上。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know if there's a story here, but I want there to be.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不知道这里面有没有故事，但我希望有。

sentences.en: But there are little cool things about bikers.
sentences.zh: 但拜克确实有一些很酷的小东西。

sentences.en: There's actually a lot that's kind of neat about it.
sentences.zh: 实际上它有很多不错的地方。

sentences.en: Ralph Erskine, the architect, he was a socialist and a Quaker and he really wanted to build a place that fostered community.
sentences.zh: 建筑师拉尔夫·厄斯金是一位社会主义者和贵格会教徒，他真心想建造一个促进社区感的地方。

sentences.en: And he'd also studied buildings in the Arctic and how they were constructed to sort of shield the inner courtyards from winds coming in from the outside.
sentences.zh: 他还研究过北极的建筑，以及它们是如何建造来保护内部庭院免受外部风吹的。

sentences.en: And he wanted to do something similar, but not just to shield it from winds, but also just to enclose the residents in this vulvic community.
sentences.zh: 他想做类似的事情，不仅是为了挡风，也是为了把居民包围在这个阴道式的社区里。

sentences.en: And Erskine tried really, really hard to involve a bunch of the residents from the old biker in the redesign of the new one.
sentences.zh: 厄斯金非常非常努力地让旧拜克的许多居民参与到新拜克的重新设计中。

sentences.en: But despite his sort of best efforts, not that many of the original residents ended up living there.
sentences.zh: 但尽管他尽了最大努力，最终并没有多少原居民住进去。

sentences.en: And eventually in the 80s, the place kind of turns a little bit back into a slum.
sentences.zh: 最终在80年代，这个地方又有点变回了贫民窟。

sentences.en: There's a lot of crime and vacancies and a lot of the places sort of fall into disrepair.
sentences.zh: 有很多犯罪和空房，很多地方陷入了失修状态。

sentences.en: The Guardian said this about the biker, the new biker estate.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》是这样评价拜克，即新的拜克住宅区的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For all its faults, biker wall was an exemplar of both design and an attempt to involve the community in the changes planned for them by those in power.
sentences.zh: 尽管有种种缺陷，拜克之墙既是设计的典范，也是让社区参与到当权者为他们规划的变革中的一次尝试。

sentences.en: That it failed in so many ways reveals that it's rarely in the interests of communities to demolish the homes they live in.
sentences.zh: 它在许多方面失败了，这表明拆除人们居住的家园很少符合社区的利益。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's to me, that's just sort of like you can try really hard to do it right and it still might come out wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这就像是，你可以非常努力地去做对，但结果可能还是会出错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, and Beatrix Campbell, the YouTube lady, she admits that the place is flawed, but she still thinks it's pretty great.
sentences.zh: 所以，比阿特丽克斯·坎贝尔，那位YouTube女士，她承认这个地方有缺陷，但她仍然认为它很棒。

sentences.en: It's flawed, of course, but at least unlike most of its contemporaries, there's a bit of democracy here.
sentences.zh: 它当然有缺陷，但至少与大多数同时代的建筑不同，这里有一点民主。

sentences.en: It's both monumental and modeSt.
sentences.zh: 它既宏伟又谦逊。

sentences.en: It's a social space and domestic.
sentences.zh: 它既是社交空间又是生活空间。

sentences.en: There's something lighthearted about this place.
sentences.zh: 这个地方有一些轻松愉快的东西。

sentences.en: There's something lovable.
sentences.zh: 有一些可爱的东西。

sentences.en: Okay, so I don't know if you could understand her last line there, but she says there's something lighthearted about this place, something lovable.
sentences.zh: 好的，我不知道你是否听懂了她最后那句话，但她说这个地方有一些轻松愉快的东西，一些可爱的东西。

sentences.en: And then I love that if you scroll down just a little ways, the comment on the video says they didn't tell them it was Carl Orff 24-7 in this place.
sentences.zh: 然后我喜欢的是，如果你往下翻一点，视频评论里说他们没告诉他们这个地方24小时都在放卡尔·奥尔夫的音乐。

sentences.en: I think what that comment is getting at is that it was really kind of a dark place to live because Carl Orff wrote this tune.
sentences.zh: 我想那条评论的意思是，住在这里真的很压抑，因为卡尔·奥尔夫写了这首曲子。

sentences.en: And that's pretty dark.
sentences.zh: 那真的很压抑。

sentences.en: It's the biker wall.
sentences.zh: 这就是拜克之墙。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Thank you, Katie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，凯蒂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: In 2014, the Biker Community Trust started a multi-million dollar revamp of the biker wall with lots of improvements, including broadband in every property.
sentences.zh: 2014年，拜克社区信托基金开始对拜克之墙进行数百万美元的翻新，进行了许多改进，包括每处房产都接入了宽带。

sentences.en: So I hope it's not all Carl Orff up there anymore, if indeed it ever was.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望那里不再全是卡尔·奥尔夫的音乐了，如果确实曾经有过的话。

sentences.en: Tell me who you are.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你是谁。

sentences.en: I am Sharif Youssef, assistant producer at 99PI.
sentences.zh: 我是谢里夫·优素福，99PI的助理制片人。

sentences.en: And what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: What do you do?
sentences.zh: 你是做什么的？

sentences.en: I sort of do a lot of the Pro Tools stuff, so working with the actual tape for a lot of the producer's stories.
sentences.zh: 我主要负责很多Pro Tools的工作，也就是处理制片人故事中实际的录音带。

sentences.en: I score and sound design a lot of the pieces.
sentences.zh: 我为很多片段配乐和做声音设计。

sentences.en: I do research and fact-checking.
sentences.zh: 我做研究和事实核查。

sentences.en: So I basically do whatever needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上是哪里需要就去哪里。

sentences.en: And so what is your mini-story?
sentences.zh: 那么你的迷你故事是什么？

sentences.en: So things that are creative are relatively simple to copyright.
sentences.zh: 创造性的东西相对容易获得版权。

sentences.en: You write a song, copyright.
sentences.zh: 你写了一首歌，有版权。

sentences.en: You write a book.
sentences.zh: 你写了一本书。

sentences.en: It's easy to get copyright, and it's easy to prove that you've done this thing.
sentences.zh: 获得版权很容易，证明你做了这件事也很容易。

sentences.en: But a question arises when you try to copyright something that is based in fact some sort of objective reality,
sentences.zh: 但当你试图为某种基于事实、某种客观现实的东西申请版权时，问题就出现了，

sentences.en: like the definition of a word in dictionaries or an entry for a person in an encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 就像字典里对单词的定义，或者百科全书中对某人的条目一样。

sentences.en: Or, in this case, maps, when I know you like a good map story.
sentences.zh: 或者，在这个案例中，是地图，因为我知道你喜欢精彩的地图故事。

sentences.en: Oh, I love a good map story.
sentences.zh: 哦，我最喜欢精彩的地图故事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this story is about a town called Aglo, New York.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事是关于纽约州一个叫阿格洛（Aglo）的小镇。

sentences.en: And it was in the 1930s, the General Drafting Company was creating a map of New York State.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪30年代，通用制图公司（General Drafting Company）正在绘制纽约州的地图。

sentences.en: So they put in a lot of hours and a lot of manpower detailing all the rivers and gorges and Finger Lakes and towns.
sentences.zh: 他们投入了大量的时间和人力，详细描绘了所有的河流、峡谷、五指湖和城镇。

sentences.en: And they said, we put in so much work, you know, we have to protect our investment.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们投入了这么多心血，必须保护我们的投资成果。

sentences.en: So they set a copyright trap near the northwest corner of Pennsylvania, just a couple miles into New York.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们在宾夕法尼亚州西北角附近，也就是刚进入纽约州几英里的地方，设置了一个版权陷阱。

sentences.en: They put a little town next to Roscoe, New York, called Aglo.
sentences.zh: 他们在纽约州罗斯科（Roscoe）旁边放了一个叫阿格洛的小镇。

sentences.en: And Aglo, I believe, is actually a jumble of the initials of the founders' names, A-G-L-O-E.
sentences.zh: 我相信，阿格洛实际上是创始人名字首字母的组合，即A-G-L-O-E。

sentences.en: And so they put this on the map, and they know that if another map shows Aglo, New York, that person was copying their map.
sentences.zh: 他们把这个名字放进地图里，这样如果另一张地图上也出现了纽约州的阿格洛，他们就知道那个人抄袭了他们的地图。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So they create this fictitious town.
sentences.zh: 所以他们创造了这个虚构的小镇。

sentences.en: It's on the map.
sentences.zh: 它出现在了地图上。

sentences.en: And it's like sold in Esso stations around the state.
sentences.zh: 而且它在全州的埃索（Esso）加油站都有售。

sentences.en: And for a while, everything is all hunky-dory.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，一切都相安无事。

sentences.en: But then, several years later, another map comes out.
sentences.zh: 但几年后，另一张地图出版了。

sentences.en: And they open the map, and lo and behold, Aglo was on it.
sentences.zh: 他们打开地图一看，嘿，你猜怎么着，阿格洛竟然在上面。

sentences.en: This company was called Rand McNally Drafting Company.
sentences.zh: 这家公司叫兰德麦克纳利制图公司（Rand McNally Drafting Company）。

sentences.en: Busted.
sentences.zh: 被抓住了。

sentences.en: Busted.
sentences.zh: 被抓住了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what they thought.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他们当时也是这么想的。

sentences.en: So the general drafting company goes, yo, Rand McNally, you stole our map, and we're going to sue you.
sentences.zh: 于是通用制图公司说，嘿，兰德麦克纳利，你们偷了我们的地图，我们要起诉你们。

sentences.en: And Rand McNally is like, no, no, wait, this is an actual place.
sentences.zh: 兰德麦克纳利却说，不，不，等等，这是一个真实存在的地方。

sentences.en: Let's go and take a look.
sentences.zh: 我们去看看吧。

sentences.en: And so the general drafting company people are like, okay, sure, take us to Aglo.
sentences.zh: 通用制图公司的人说，好啊，没问题，带我们去阿格洛看看。

sentences.en: So they go to this place where Aglo should be.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了阿格洛本该在的地方。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, there is actually a big general store there, a small general store, actually.
sentences.zh: 结果你猜怎么着，那里真的有一家大型杂货店，准确地说，是一家小型杂货店。

sentences.en: And it's called the Aglo General Store.
sentences.zh: 它叫阿格洛杂货店。

sentences.en: And there are a couple houses, maybe two at its peak.
sentences.zh: 那里还有几栋房子，鼎盛时期大概有两栋。

sentences.en: And so the story goes, some people, maybe from the neighboring towns, wandered to this place,
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，有些人，可能是从邻近城镇来的，游荡到了这个地方，

sentences.en: wanted to build a general store, saw that the map said Aglo is here, but nothing was there.
sentences.zh: 想要建一家杂货店，看到地图上写着阿格洛在这里，但当时什么都没有。

sentences.en: So when they wanted to build the store, they just slapped on the Aglo name.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们想建店时，就直接用了阿格洛这个名字。

sentences.en: So this place that was created as a fictitious copyright trap sort of sprang up into reality.
sentences.zh: 于是，这个原本作为虚构版权陷阱而创造的地方，就这样变成了现实。

sentences.en: So this sort of became famous because this author, John Green, wrote a book called Paper Towns that is set in Aglo, New York.
sentences.zh: 这个故事之所以出名，是因为作家约翰·格林（John Green）写了一本名为《纸镇》（Paper Towns）的书，故事背景就设在纽约州的阿格洛。

sentences.en: And he gave a TEDx talk about Aglo, New York and about the concept of Paper Towns as well.
sentences.zh: 他还做了一场关于纽约州阿格洛以及“纸镇”概念的TEDx演讲。

sentences.en: And it was since turned into a movie.
sentences.zh: 后来这个故事还被改编成了电影。

sentences.en: So we thought this story might not be a great fit for us because people in our audience might already be really familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得这个故事可能不太适合我们，因为我们的听众可能已经非常熟悉了。

sentences.en: But we can talk about it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以稍微聊聊它。

sentences.en: And if you want to learn more, you should look up John Green because he and his brother, Hank, make these great videos.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解更多，你应该去搜搜约翰·格林，因为他和他的兄弟汉克（Hank）制作了这些很棒的视频。

sentences.en: You learn all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你可以学到各种各样的知识。

sentences.en: I know people who like this show will totally love what they do on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我知道喜欢我们节目的听众一定会喜欢他们在YouTube上做的事情。

sentences.en: So check them out.
sentences.zh: 去看看吧。

sentences.en: And you are?
sentences.zh: 那么你是谁？

sentences.en: I'm Kurt Colstead and I'm the digital director at 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 我是库尔特·科尔斯特德（Kurt Colstead），我是《99%隐形》（99% Invisible）的数字总监。

sentences.en: And describe what that means.
sentences.zh: 描述一下那意味着什么。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: I produce web stories for the show and I take care of all of our digital content.
sentences.zh: 我为节目制作网络故事，并负责我们所有的数字内容。

sentences.en: So several years ago, I remember being in the waiting room waiting for Maslow, who was in surgery.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我记得当时在候诊室等马斯洛（Maslow），他正在做手术。

sentences.en: It all turned out fine.
sentences.zh: 结果一切顺利。

sentences.en: I got an email from a firefighter and she said, do you know anything about Knox boxes, which are these little invisible elements that you see everywhere in urban environments,
sentences.zh: 我收到了一位消防员的电子邮件，她说，你知道诺克斯箱（Knox box）吗？那是你在城市环境中随处可见的小型隐形元素，

sentences.en: but you probably never notice them.
sentences.zh: 但你可能从来没注意过它们。

sentences.en: So please tell us what is a Knox box.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我们，什么是诺克斯箱。

sentences.en: Yeah, Knox box in simple terms is a rapid entry system.
sentences.zh: 好的，简单来说，诺克斯箱是一种快速进入系统。

sentences.en: It allows emergency personnel to get into buildings quickly when there's a disaster going on.
sentences.zh: 它允许紧急救援人员在发生灾难时快速进入建筑物。

sentences.en: So, for example, when there's a fire in your apartment building and the fire department is trying to get in quickly, they show up, they open the Knox box,
sentences.zh: 例如，当你的公寓大楼发生火灾，消防部门试图快速进入时，他们赶到现场，打开诺克斯箱，

sentences.en: get out a key and enter the building.
sentences.zh: 取出钥匙，然后进入大楼。

sentences.en: So describe it like physically.
sentences.zh: 描述一下它的外观。

sentences.en: So it's like a little box that's sort of up against a wall, like posted on a wall.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个小盒子，贴在墙上，挂在墙上那种。

sentences.en: A Knox box will typically be found within a few feet of an entryway.
sentences.zh: 诺克斯箱通常位于入口几英尺范围内。

sentences.en: It's an eye level.
sentences.zh: 它在视线高度。

sentences.en: It's a black box usually with a little red on it.
sentences.zh: 它通常是一个黑色的盒子，上面有一点红色。

sentences.en: So it's easy to spot.
sentences.zh: 所以很容易发现。

sentences.en: So the fire department shows up.
sentences.zh: 消防部门赶到现场。

sentences.en: They grab ahold of this little box and they use their master key to open it and enter the building.
sentences.zh: 他们抓住这个小盒子，用他们的万能钥匙打开它，然后进入大楼。

sentences.en: So if there's a fire inside, they don't want to break in and all the doors and windows.
sentences.zh: 如果里面有火灾，他们不想破门破窗。

sentences.en: They just, if there's a key available, they can use it.
sentences.zh: 如果能拿到钥匙，他们就可以直接使用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In an emergency, they're not worried about, you know, the property damage.
sentences.zh: 在紧急情况下，他们不会担心财产损失。

sentences.en: Of course, that's a byproduct.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是副产品。

sentences.en: But they're worried about injuring themselves, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们担心的是自己受伤，对吧？

sentences.en: So if they have to break a glass door and jump through that glass door, that puts them at greater risk.
sentences.zh: 如果他们必须打破玻璃门并跳进去，那会让他们面临更大的风险。

sentences.en: It also takes more time to get into the building.
sentences.zh: 进入大楼也需要更多时间。

sentences.en: This saves them time, reduces injury risk, and just lets them in quickly.
sentences.zh: 这能为他们节省时间，降低受伤风险，并让他们快速进入。

sentences.en: And so how does the whole system work?
sentences.zh: 那么整个系统是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: So they have a master key that opens up all the Knox boxes?
sentences.zh: 他们有一把能打开所有诺克斯箱的万能钥匙吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So their master key opens up all the Knox boxes for all the different buildings.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的万能钥匙可以打开所有不同建筑的诺克斯箱。

sentences.en: And that means when they arrive at a building, they don't have to sort through a bunch of keys,
sentences.zh: 这意味着当他们到达一栋建筑时，不必在一堆钥匙里翻找，

sentences.en: figure out how they're going to get into that particular building.
sentences.zh: 也不用费心去想怎么进入那栋特定的建筑。

sentences.en: They just whip out their one key, stick it in the Knox box, open it up.
sentences.zh: 他们只需掏出那把钥匙，插进诺克斯箱，打开它。

sentences.en: And inside of that, they will find whatever key they need to access that particular building.
sentences.zh: 在里面，他们会找到进入该建筑所需的任何钥匙。

sentences.en: Where does the name Knox come from?
sentences.zh: 诺克斯这个名字是怎么来的？

sentences.en: Knox is a company that produces a lot of these boxes.
sentences.zh: 诺克斯是一家生产很多这种盒子的公司。

sentences.en: And so technically, generically, you might call them a rapid entry system.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，泛指的话，你可以称它们为快速进入系统。

sentences.en: But Knox makes so many of them that it has become an everyday sort of household name for these things.
sentences.zh: 但诺克斯生产的太多了，以至于它已经成为这些东西的日常代名词。

sentences.en: Knox box.
sentences.zh: 诺克斯箱。

sentences.en: Like Kleenex.
sentences.zh: 就像舒洁（Kleenex）一样。

sentences.en: It's like Band-Aid and Kleenex.
sentences.zh: 就像邦迪（Band-Aid）和舒洁一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: So like if you were in any populated area, you will see a ton of these, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在任何人口稠密的地区，你会看到很多这种东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们随处可见。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You are surrounded by Knox boxes basically anywhere you go.
sentences.zh: 无论你走到哪里，基本上都被诺克斯箱包围着。

sentences.en: You probably pass a dozen or so of these just walking down the street every day.
sentences.zh: 你每天走在街上，可能都会经过十几个这样的东西。

sentences.en: So on every block of every city, you'll find some equivalent of a Knox box attached to the outside of the building.
sentences.zh: 所以每个城市的每个街区，你都会发现建筑物外墙上贴着某种形式的诺克斯箱。

sentences.en: And once you start seeing these, you will see them everywhere.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始留意，你就会发现它们无处不在。

sentences.en: They are at a high level.
sentences.zh: 它们安装在较高位置。

sentences.en: They're made to be seen.
sentences.zh: 它们就是为了被看到而设计的。

sentences.en: And yet they're somehow strangely invisible until you start noticing them.
sentences.zh: 然而，在你开始注意到它们之前，它们在某种程度上又是奇怪地隐形的。

sentences.en: So cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: This was one of those great examples of a short story that was just, it's an anecdote more than a story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的短篇故事例子，与其说是故事，不如说是一则轶事。

sentences.en: So it made sense to just put it up on the web and call it good.
sentences.zh: 所以把它放到网上，就这样结束是很合理的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we have tons of those.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多这样的故事。

sentences.en: We have a whole website devoted to them at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 我们在99pi.org上有一个专门的网站来展示它们。

sentences.en: Thanks to Nikki, the former firefighter, for the Knox box suggestion all those years ago.
sentences.zh: 感谢前消防员尼基（Nikki）多年前提出的诺克斯箱建议。

sentences.en: Last week, I got this mini story suggestion from Tucson, Arizona resident Megan Phillips.
sentences.zh: 上周，我收到了来自亚利桑那州图森市居民梅根·菲利普斯（Megan Phillips）的迷你故事建议。

sentences.en: In Tucson, roads running east-west are called street.
sentences.zh: 在图森，东西向的道路被称为“街”（street）。

sentences.en: Roads running north-south are called avenue.
sentences.zh: 南北向的道路被称为“大道”（avenue）。

sentences.en: That all makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这都说得通。

sentences.en: But what is unique to Tucson is that any diagonal roads are called stravenue, a portmanteau of street and avenue.
sentences.zh: 但图森独特之处在于，任何对角线道路都被称为“stravenue”，这是“street”和“avenue”的合成词。

sentences.en: That is an official designation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个官方称呼。

sentences.en: It's not just slang.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是俚语。

sentences.en: And I think that's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺酷的。

sentences.en: When I got Megan's note, I was sitting next to famous portmanteau skeptic Helen Saltzman of The IllusioniSt.
sentences.zh: 当我收到梅根的便条时，我正坐在《幻觉师》（The Illusionist）节目的著名合成词怀疑论者海伦·萨尔茨曼（Helen Saltzman）旁边。

sentences.en: That's Radiotopia's acclaimed word podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是Radiotopia旗下备受赞誉的词汇播客。

sentences.en: And I asked her what she thought.
sentences.zh: 我问了她的看法。

sentences.en: I know your general opinion, portmanteau, is pretty negative.
sentences.zh: 我知道你对合成词的总体看法相当负面。

sentences.en: I think that's unfair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不公平。

sentences.en: I think where portmanteaus are useful is to express a concept for which you don't have a proper term.
sentences.zh: 我认为合成词的用处在于表达一个你没有合适术语的概念。

sentences.en: And it's related to concepts that you do already have terms for.
sentences.zh: 而且它与你已经有术语的概念相关。

sentences.en: However, in this case, I feel like the portmanteau is fixing a problem that doesn't really exiSt.
sentences.zh: 然而，在这种情况下，我觉得这个合成词是在解决一个并不真正存在的问题。

sentences.en: And that problem is that the people of Tucson are just very much too dependent on things either being streets or avenues.
sentences.zh: 那个问题就是图森的人们太依赖于事物要么是街，要么是大道的分类了。

sentences.en: And I come from Britain, which does not have such a binary road naming system.
sentences.zh: 我来自英国，那里没有这种二元化的道路命名系统。

sentences.en: So you might get a street that is called a street or a road or an avenue or a crescent or a boulevard or not even have a road term at all.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会遇到一条路，它被称为街、路、大道、新月路、林荫大道，甚至根本没有道路后缀。

sentences.en: And it could go in any direction.
sentences.zh: 而且它可以朝任何方向延伸。

sentences.en: So live and let live, Tucson.
sentences.zh: 所以，图森，各安天命吧。

sentences.en: It's a very pro-design, pro-grid show.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常推崇设计、推崇网格的节目。

sentences.en: I'm sorry that you had to hear that, my nerds.
sentences.zh: 很抱歉让你们听到了这些，我的书呆子们。

sentences.en: But I assure you, Helen Saltzman's The Illusionist is a fantastic podcast that will teach and entertain you about words and the strange consequences of language.
sentences.zh: 但我向你们保证，海伦·萨尔茨曼的《幻觉师》是一个很棒的播客，它会教导并娱乐你，让你了解词汇以及语言的奇妙后果。

sentences.en: But I won't have Helen planning my city because grids rule.
sentences.zh: 但我不会让海伦来规划我的城市，因为网格才是王道。

sentences.en: Man, I'm so excited to – I was about to say I'm so excited to get this story out of my system.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我太兴奋了——我刚才想说我太兴奋了，终于把这个故事讲出来了。

sentences.en: But honestly, I still think it would make a good story.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，我仍然认为它会是一个好故事。

sentences.en: I think everyone is wrong and I think I'm right and I want it to – I'm still holding out hope.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每个人都错了，我觉得我是对的，我想——我仍然抱有希望。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Maybe there would be a groundswell that they need to know the whole story at the end.
sentences.zh: 也许会有一股浪潮，让他们在最后知道整个故事。

sentences.en: Maybe, maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，也许吧。

sentences.en: Or I'm just worried that people will hear it and be like, oh, yeah, no, it doesn't work, which would mean I'm totally crazy.
sentences.zh: 或者我只是担心人们听了之后会说，哦，是啊，不，这行不通，那意味着我完全疯了。

sentences.en: Let's find out.
sentences.zh: 让我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me who you are.
sentences.zh: 好的，告诉我你是谁。

sentences.en: I'm Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 我是艾弗里·特鲁夫曼（Avery Truffleman）。

sentences.en: What do you do here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里做什么？

sentences.en: I'm a producer at 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 我是《99%隐形》的制作人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're telling all the type of stories that we can't tell on the radio for various reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们正在讲述各种因为种种原因无法在广播中播出的故事。

sentences.en: Maybe they were little parts of stories that got cut out because they were too confusing.
sentences.zh: 也许它们只是故事中因为太令人困惑而被删减的小片段。

sentences.en: Then you pass.

sentences.en: And I went to a bunch of ophthalmologists and I took this vision test a bunch of times.

sentences.en: It's what everybody has.

sentences.en: And a big part of why the Snellen chart works really well is because it's easy to memorize.
sentences.zh: 斯内伦视力表之所以好用，很大一部分原因在于它很容易背下来。

sentences.en: And a lot of ophthalmologists and eye doctors have memorized their chart.

sentences.en: And they can assess you really quickly.

sentences.en: Which if you're an eye doctor, you're doing this to every single patient.
sentences.zh: 如果你是眼科医生，你每天要面对每一位病人。

sentences.en: And then this adds minutes to your day once you have it memorized.
sentences.zh: 一旦背下来，这能为你每天节省不少时间。

sentences.en: But if every line has a different amount of letters on it, it's basically a different test every time.
sentences.zh: 但如果每一行的字母数量都不同，那基本上每次测试都不一样。

sentences.zh: 你的概率也不同。

sentences.zh: 如果你在20/20那一行读对了五个中的三个，你就会被判定为20/20视力。

sentences.zh: 这简直是不精确得离谱。

sentences.en: It's unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直难以置信。

sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: That is Dr. Ian Bailey.
sentences.zh: 那位是Ian Bailey医生。

sentences.en: And in the 70s, he helped design a more precise vision chart that has five letters on every single line.
sentences.zh: 在70年代，他参与设计了一种更精确的视力表，每一行都有五个字母。

sentences.en: I think our chart design could be compared with designing a ruler where you say, why don't we make the markings along the ruler of the same size?
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们的视力表设计可以比作设计一把尺子，你会问，为什么我们不把尺子上的刻度做得一样大呢？

sentences.en: It seems obvious.
sentences.zh: 这似乎显而易见。

sentences.en: And so he has five big letters at the top, five letters on the next line, five letters on the next line, all spaced equally apart.
sentences.zh: 所以他在最上面放了五个大字母，下一行五个，再下一行五个，所有字母的间距都相等。

sentences.en: It's very precise.
sentences.zh: 非常精确。

sentences.en: But if you visualize it for a second, right, instead of one giant letter at the top, there are five giant letters at the top, which means that it is a physically bigger chart.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想象一下，最上面不是一个巨大的字母，而是五个巨大的字母，这意味着它在物理上是一张更大的表。

sentences.en: It's just wider.
sentences.zh: 它更宽。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: But there's still always five.
sentences.zh: 但每一行始终都有五个。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: And then the thing is he also had to pick which letters to use.
sentences.zh: 还有一点是，他还得挑选使用哪些字母。

sentences.en: And so some letters are more confusable, like C and G.
sentences.zh: 有些字母更容易混淆，比如C和G。

sentences.en: Some letters are very distinct, like Z and A.
sentences.zh: 有些字母非常独特，比如Z和A。

sentences.en: And so he also had this like design challenge of making sure that you wouldn't have one line of like, oh,
sentences.zh: 所以他还要面临一个设计挑战，确保不会出现一行全是简单字母，而另一行全是困难字母的情况，要确保它们分布均匀。

sentences.en: easy letters and one line of difficult letters to make sure they distribute evenly.
sentences.zh: 他还得确保，因为他是在澳大利亚设计的，他要确保N和Z不会挨在一起，因为人们会联想到……

sentences.en: And he also had to make sure that there wasn't like, because he designed it in Australia and he wanted to make sure N and Z weren't next to each other because people would be like,
sentences.zh: 哦，新西兰（New Zealand）。

sentences.en: oh, New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 从而产生对形状的联想。

sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这确实是一张很难设计的视力表。

sentences.zh: 但问题是，这张表确实大得多，也宽得多。
